### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **68** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-instances.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-instances.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f797f5d07ebadc911000ee311aa3f80bcdab8ff9` — the merge of head `35a988b6bba31b9973c95fb5c2f0798fc213f3ec` into base `f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f797f5d07ebadc911000ee311aa3f80bcdab8ff9 && git checkout f797f5d07ebadc911000ee311aa3f80bcdab8ff9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b 35a988b6bba31b9973c95fb5c2f0798fc213f3ec && git checkout -B drift-repro f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b && git merge --no-ff 35a988b6bba31b9973c95fb5c2f0798fc213f3ec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

# Contract review brief — #31699 narrowing PR (connector, last PR of ADR-0150 child B)

Reviewer: an isolated agent with no part in writing the change. Read the code, not the author's summary, and judge it yourself.

## What to read

- The change: `git -C /home/user/objectstack-issue-31699 show 4a9d32b9` (one commit on `origin/main` df9fe946). Read every hunk, and the surrounding code where a hunk's correctness depends on it.
- The changeset in that commit: `.changeset/31699-connector-names-per-namespace.md`. Its `Clause-②` line must list every answer that moves for a caller that worked before, each with FROM and TO.
- The PR body draft: `/mnt/project-files/server-seat-7/r2026-11-14/31699-narrow-body.md`.
- The card's requirements: GitHub issue objectstack-ai/objectstack#31699, comments 6871869590 (handover, "The narrowing PR" list), 6879929803 (addendum), 6816295828 and 6820178514 (a disabled holder at the connector dispatch door: "resolve and count over one holder set, the served set"), 6882996364 (this PR's file surface and its one stated deviation).
- ADR-0150 (`docs/adr/0150-*.md` in the worktree), especially D2, D3, D4, D9, D10 and the epic red lines:
  1. Resolution never loosens: no caller is served an item it could not reach before, and no other package's body is served or sent.
  2. Ambiguity is reported, never guessed: two candidates are refused naming both, never one picked by order.
  3. Each PR is independently releasable: a one-holder deployment's answers do not move unless the changeset declares it.
- The precedent narrowing for `webhook` (merged as e55347d21, changeset `.changeset/31699-webhook-names-per-namespace.md` in git history) for the expected shape of the declaration.

## What to judge

1. Red lines 1 to 3 across every reader that names a connector: the reconcile (materialization, refusal of an entry with no package of its own, duplicate checks, the no-registry composition), the engine's `resolveConnectorInstanceFor` (every arm, including the plugin code-registered exception and the disabled-only arm), the `connector_action` dispatch, the connector pull (connector resolved from the mapping's package; provider, origin, degraded state, handler and inputSchema read from that one instance), the connection door (bare and namespace address; `request.package`; the recorded package of a begun connect), the OAuth2 grant handles keyed by instance, the credential listing, descriptors.
2. A disabled holder, in both registration orders, at every door that serves or dispatches.
3. Whether anything still keyed by bare name can mix two packages' instances (maps, caches, log keys, the materializer's retry timers, the credential-refusal map, `grantHandles`).
4. The completeness and truth of the changeset's FROM → TO list and its one-holder sentence, against the code.
5. Whether the tests pin what they claim (look for vacuous pins), and whether an important path has no pin.
6. The stated deviation (namespace address instead of `?package=`): acceptable or not, and why.

## Output

Write the report to `/mnt/project-files/server-seat-7/r2026-11-14/31699-narrow-review-r1.md` and return it. Format:

- Verdict: PASS, PASS-WITH-CHANGES, or FAIL.
- Must-fix (blocks landing), should-fix, nits: each with file:line, the concrete failing scenario (inputs → wrong answer), and the fix.
- A short Clause-② judgement: is `yes (narrowing)` right, and is every moved answer listed.

Do not edit the worktree, push, or post anywhere. Running tests read-only is fine (`cd packages/services/service-automation && npx vitest run <file>`), but do not leave files changed.

# Contract review r1 — #31699 narrowing PR (connector), commit 4a9d32b9

Reviewer: isolated agent, no part in the change. Read: every hunk of 4a9d32b9, the changeset, the PR body draft, issue comments 6871869590, 6879929803, 6816295828, 6820178514, 6882996364, and the surrounding code the hunks depend on. Five claims below were measured with probe tests run from a scratch directory against the worktree's source (nothing in the worktree was written; `git status` is clean at 4a9d32b9). Each finding says whether it was run or only read.

## Verdict: PASS-WITH-CHANGES

Red lines 1 and 2 hold on every path I traced: I found no caller served or sent another package's instance, and no instance picked by order. Two defects block landing: one answer moves for a one-holder deployment without being declared (red line 3), and one bare-name key still mixes two packages' instances.

## Must-fix

### M1. The credential listing loses `state` and `degradedReason` for a one-holder instance whose entry carries a sentinel stamp (red line 3, undeclared)

- Where: `packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts:5159-5163` (`declaredCredentialRefs` keeps the raw `_packageId`) and `plugin.ts:5196-5200` (`descriptorOf` matches `d.packageId === c.packageId`).
- Scenario (run): one declared provider-bound entry `billing` with `_packageId: 'sys_metadata'` (the environment's stored row) or `'__runtime__'` (the compatibility default), credential missing. The instance registers under the package `connectorInstancePackage` gives it (none, or the name's holder), so its descriptor carries no `packageId`, or the holder's.
  - FROM (main): `listConnectorCredentialRefs()` answers `connectors: [{ name: 'billing', packageId: 'sys_metadata', state: 'degraded', degradedReason: … }]` (the descriptor was found by name).
  - TO (this commit, measured): `connectors: [{ name: 'billing', packageId: 'sys_metadata' }]`. Same for `'__runtime__'`.
- This is a one-holder answer that moves, and the changeset's one-holder sentence does not list it.
- Fix: look the descriptor up by the instance's package, not the raw stamp: `connectorInstancePackage(resolve, entry)` (or at least `declaredEntryPackage`), `null` matching a descriptor with no `packageId`. Add a pin with a `sys_metadata` entry, and one with two packages' instances in different states (the changeset claims the per-instance listing and nothing pins it).

### M2. The reload merge supersedes by bare name, so a reload of one package's artifact tears down another package's instance of the name

- Where: `plugin.ts:1329-1335` (`mergeDeclaredConnectorSources`): a registry entry is dropped when `declaredNames.has(name)`, whatever its package.
- Scenario (the merge was run; the consequences below are read from the reconcile): host package `com.acme.host` and installed package `com.acme.beta` (another namespace) each declare a provider-bound `billing`; both are materialized. A `metadata:reloaded` payload of the host's artifact carries `connectors: [billing]`.
  - Stamped payload item: the merge returns only the host's entry. `com.acme.beta/billing` is no longer desired, so the reconcile dematerializes it, and `reloadedConnectors` persists, so every later reconcile and the connection door (`readDeclaredConnectorItems`) omit it until restart. Beta's flows fail "no handler", and its namespace door answers 404.
  - Unstamped payload item (the existing control at `connector-materialization.test.ts:1115` shows this shape is supported): the merge returns one entry with no package of its own. Under two holders `connectorInstanceRefusal` refuses it, so both instances are gone after the reload.
- It fails closed (nothing is served to the wrong caller), but it is exactly the bare-name mixing the brief asks about, and the two-holder state is opened by this PR.
- Fix: supersede by `(package, name)`: drop a registry entry only when the artifact re-declares its name under the same package, or under one of `owners` for an unstamped item; treat an unstamped artifact item as its manifest's package (`owners`) rather than as an entry with no package. Pin: two holders, reload of one package's artifact, the other's instance still dispatches.

## Should-fix

### S1. A caller inside the disabled package is still served its own instance; the changeset, docblock, docs and one test title say "no caller"

- Where: `engine.ts:5946-5959`. The registry keeps the caller's own holding in the served set (`objectql/src/registry.ts:9535-9537`), so `resolver(name, A)` is `resolved` (own) for a disabled `A`, and the `resolved` arm returns A's instance while it is registered.
- Scenario (run): A and B hold `billing`, both instances registered, A disabled: `resolveConnectorInstanceFor('billing', A)` is `{ status: 'instance', packageId: A }`. Same with A the lone holder.
- This is main's answer, and it is the package's own body, so no red line breaks. But it is the exact case note 6816295828 names ("a flow of a disabled package"), and nothing pins it: the tests at `flow-package-scoped-resolution.test.ts:932` and `:961` use `P` (a dependent of A) as "A's own caller", and the second is titled "served to no caller".
- Not true as written: changeset item (7) "for every caller"; the docblock "a disabled package's instance is never served"; the docs line "its instance is never served".
- Fix: either answer `codeRegisteredInstance` when the resolved package holder is disabled (then every statement is true), or keep the answer, say so in the three places, and pin caller = A in both registration orders.

### S2. Changeset item (5) gives the wrong FROM for catalog holders beside a plugin's connector

- Scenario (run): A and B each declare a catalog entry `slack` (no provider), a plugin registers `slack` in code. `resolveConnectorInstanceFor('slack', null)` is `refused`; for caller A it is the plugin's instance.
- FROM (main, a boot-sealed clash): an environment-authored flow dispatched the plugin's connector (the one instance of the name). TO: refused naming both. Item (5) says FROM "not dispatched as not registered".
- Fix: add the row to the changeset. Or decide that a name whose every candidate has no instance of its own answers the plugin's connector for a caller with no package too, since every package caller already gets it.

### S3. Holders the namespace address cannot tell apart are now materialized, and no HTTP door reaches them

- The reconcile no longer refuses two stamped entries of one name, whatever their namespaces (`plugin.ts:3402-3432`). The install door still refuses a same-namespace co-owner and a namespace-less package, but a cold boot only warns (`BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE` `'warn'`).
- Scenario (read, not run): two code-declared packages of one namespace both declare provider-bound `crm` with `authorization_code`. FROM: boot refused naming both. TO: both materialized; the bare door is 409, and `/connectors/NS/crm/connection` is 409 `ambiguous-in-namespace` (`automation-address.ts:300-302`). Neither can be connected over HTTP. `?package=` would have reached them.
- The docs say such holders "still may not" coexist, which is true only of the install door.
- Fix: either keep the reconcile's refusal for holders the namespace rule does not admit (the boot answer then does not move for them), or state in the changeset and docs that they materialize and are connectable only in process (`request.package`).

### S4. "The reconcile drops a disabled package's instance on its next run" does not cover an entry with no package of its own (read, not run)

- `connectorInstancePackage` judges over every holder (`includeDisabledPackages`), and `listItems` hides only items stamped with the disabled package. An unstamped entry whose name only a disabled package D holds stays declared, is registered under D on every reconcile, and the disabled arm answers `none` for every caller, permanently rather than "until the next reconcile".
- FROM: a caller with no package dispatched it (the one instance of the name). The changeset's (7) and its BREAKING paragraph describe this as transient.
- Fix: word (7) for this case, or have the reconcile not materialize an entry whose instance package is disabled.

### S5. Missing pins on paths the brief names

- A disabled holder at the connection door under two holders: the namespace address of the disabled package (read: slot A, then 404 because A's entry is not listed), and the service's bare door (read: resolves to the enabled holder). Neither is pinned in either registration order.
- A pull whose connector has two holders, one disabled.
- The credential listing with two instances (see M1), and the reload with two holders (see M2).

## Nits

- `plugin.ts:4271`: the grant handle is keyed by the instance but reads its connection by a package re-resolved on every read. For an unstamped entry, between a second holder's install and the next reconcile, the handle of `P/name` reads as package `null`. It fails closed (read: not connected). Pass the instance's fixed `packageId`.
- `connector-connection-door.test.ts:1265`: `if (revoked) await expect(...)` asserts nothing when the handler is absent. Assert the state explicitly (not connected or degraded for CRM).
- `plugin.ts:3177`: the inert-descriptor audit builds `live` by name, so package A's catalog entry is silenced by package B's live instance of the name.
- `plugin.ts:3558` and the connect, revoke and grant-refusal log lines name the instance without its package (`inPackage` exists).
- PR body: `RESULTS_AFTER_REBASE`, `GATES_LINE` and `REVIEW_LINE` are unfilled, and "单持有者部署只变三处" needs M1's outcome.

## What I checked and found sound

- Reconcile: each stamped entry is its own instance; an entry with no package under two holders is refused naming both and registered as neither; a duplicate within a package is refused; the no-registry composition keeps one instance per name. `desired`, materialized, degraded, credential-refusal attempts and `grantHandles` are keyed by instance; unregister is by `(name, package)`. The retry timer is one global timer over all degraded instances, and `credentialRefusals` is keyed by credential ref: neither mixes instances.
- Engine: `refused` is passed through; `resolved` reads exactly the holder's instance; the plugin exception cannot return a declarative instance (`assertSameOriginOrFree` keeps the two origins off one name); the no-resolver and not-found arms answer the sole instance or `none`.
- `connector_action`: handler, degraded reason, hold, effect and inputSchema are all read by the resolved package.
- Pull: origin, degraded state, provider, handler and inputSchema are read from the one resolved instance; `refused` is 409 naming both; `none` is `connector_not_registered`. The four pins are not vacuous.
- Connection door: the recorded package wins over the addressed one; the addressed package is read exactly; `grantHandles` seed and forget by instance; the two-instance test proves two rows and two distinct tokens. N6 is judged and pinned.
- Disabled holder in both orders for a dependent caller and for a caller with no package: pinned and correct.

## The deviation (namespace address instead of `?package=`)

Acceptable. The address already exists (child G1), it is the ADR's D5 spelling, and for the state D9 admits (two holders of different namespaces) it names exactly one holder; a second spelling would add a door to keep consistent. `GET /connectors` unfiltered with `packageId` on each descriptor is additive. Its one cost is S3: holders that share a namespace or have none cannot be addressed, so the choice should come with a decision on S3.

## Clause-② judgement

`yes (narrowing)` is right. The FROM → TO list is not complete or fully true:

- Missing: M1 (a one-holder answer, so the one-holder sentence is also incomplete).
- Wrong FROM: (5) for catalog holders beside a plugin's connector (S2).
- Overstated: (7) "for every caller" (S1), and the "next run" claim in the BREAKING paragraph (S4).
- Items (1) to (4), (6), (8), (9) and (10) match the code as I read it.

# Contract review, delta after r1 — #31699 narrowing PR (connector), head de90aedb

Scope: `git diff 4a9d32b9 de90aedb` only (9 files; code changes in `service-automation/src/plugin.ts`, a docblock in `engine.ts`, tests, changeset, docs), judged against the r1 findings and for anything the delta itself breaks. Worktree not modified (`git status` clean at de90aedb).

## Verdict: PASS

No must-fix item remains, and the delta introduces none that I found.

## What was run

- The six touched or adjacent test files on de90aedb: `connector-connection-door`, `connector-materialization`, `connector-descriptor-audit`, `connector-pull`, `flow-package-scoped-resolution`, `connector-credential-door`: 329 passed, 0 failed.
- My r1 probes again, from a scratch directory:
  - M1: an entry stamped `sys_metadata` with no package holder, and one stamped `__runtime__`, each with a missing credential. The listing now answers `state: 'degraded'` and the `degradedReason` for both, with the public `packageId` still the raw stamp (main's answer).
  - M2: `mergeDeclaredConnectorSources` with a host item stamped `com.acme.host` over registry entries of `com.acme.host` and `com.acme.beta`: both entries are returned, beta's kept.
- I did not re-run the full service-automation suite or ablations A12 to A14; those are the author's figures.

## Per finding

- **M1, closed.** `declaredCredentialRefs` carries the instance's package and `descriptorOf` matches on it (`plugin.ts`, `(d.packageId ?? null) === c.instance`). The `instance` field does not reach the public answer (the mapping builds `name`, `packageId`, `state`, `degradedReason` explicitly). Dedupe by name and instance gives main's answer where two entries of one name are one instance. Both new pins assert state, not just presence.
- **M2, closed.** The merge supersedes by `(package, name)`, and the capture stamps an unstamped item with the manifest id. I checked that this id is the one the registry files the same items under: the residual rule uses `manifest.id ?? stack.id` (`spec/src/stack.zod.ts:9035`), the same expression as the capture, so a one-holder reload still replaces its own entry through `owners`. The pin proves one teardown (A's) and one materialization of B.
- **S1, closed by wording and pins.** Main's answer is kept; the changeset (7), the engine docblock and the docs now say "a caller outside the package", and caller = A is pinned in both orders and as the lone holder.
- **S2, closed.** Changeset (5) carries the plugin FROM; the new pin covers both package callers and the caller with no package.
- **S3, closed by declaration.** Changeset (2) and the docs state that a pair the install door refuses is materialized and is connectable only in process. This is a decision recorded, not a refusal; I accept it as declared.
- **S4, closed by wording.** Changeset (7), the BREAKING paragraph and the docs say the unstamped entry over a lone disabled holder is not dispatched until the package is enabled.
- **S5, closed.** New pins: bare door and CRM-addressed door with CRM disabled, both orders (404, no row written); a pull with one holder disabled; plus the M1 and M2 pins.
- **Nits, closed.** The grant handle takes the instance's fixed package (the rewritten 3b test pins that the registered instance still reads its own row and that the reconcile then materializes neither). The revoke test asserts state unconditionally. The audit judges each entry through `resolveConnectorInstanceFor` for its own package; I traced the one-holder cases (catalog entry beside a plugin connector, no plugin, no registry, an environment row) and each answers as main did. Log lines carry the package.

## Notes, none blocking

- An artifact with no manifest id and unstamped items still supersedes every entry of the name, and under two holders the reconcile then refuses that item, so both instances go on that reload. The docblock says so; the changeset bullet says only "an unstamped item is its manifest's". Worth one clause in the changeset.
- In a composition whose registry offers no package-scoped reads, a reloaded item of package H beside a registry entry of package B under one name now leaves both declared, and the reconcile refuses the second as a duplicate (main: the artifact's superseded B's). Read, not run; it needs two packages on one name with no judging registry.
- The M1 pin for `sys_metadata` covers the holder case; the no-holder and `__runtime__` cases pass in my probe but have no pin of their own.
- PR body: the three placeholders (`RESULTS_AFTER_REBASE`, `GATES_LINE`, `REVIEW_LINE`) and the one-holder count line still need filling against this head.

## Clause-② judgement

`yes (narrowing)` stands. With the reworded (2), (5) and (7), the BREAKING paragraph and the new reload and listing bullet, every moved answer I found in r1 is now either fixed back to main's answer (M1) or declared with its FROM and TO.

---

# delta-2 — head 510a8400 (`git diff de90aedb 510a8400`)

## Verdict: PASS

No must-fix item. Scope: this delta only (changeset, `plugin.ts`, one test).

- **Note 2, fixed.** `mergeDeclaredConnectorSources` supersedes by `(package, name)` only with `byPackage: true`; otherwise by name, as main did. `readDeclaredConnectorItems` computes `byPackage` with `packageScopedRegistryOf(ql.registry) !== undefined`, the same predicate the reconcile uses for `judgedByPackage`, so the merge and the reconcile agree on when two instances of a name may live. The function's only caller is that one site, and the default is the main behaviour (false).
- **Note 1, declared.** The changeset says an artifact with no manifest id, or a composition with no package-scoped registry, still supersedes by name.
- **Note 3, pinned.** The M1 environment-row pin runs for `sys_metadata` and `__runtime__`.

Run by me on 510a8400: `connector-materialization.test.ts` and `connector-descriptor-audit.test.ts`, 124 passed, 0 failed. Not re-run: the full suite (the author reports 3941) and tsc. The by-name arm for a registry with no package-scoped reads has no pin of its own; it is main's behaviour and not blocking. Worktree untouched.

Still open from the earlier record, outside this delta: the PR body placeholders and its one-holder count line.

---

# delta-3 — head e467615b, rebased on main 4ace1fa9 (conflict with #33193, b4624440)

## Verdict: PASS

No must-fix item. Scope: the conflict resolution and the new clause in changeset row (3).

**The resolution is right.** `connector` is in `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_METADATA_TYPES` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2337`), and `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` is built from it (`packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts:147`), so there is one list and the metadata hunk is docblock only. The branch's diff to `packages/spec` is that one line plus the two interface members already reviewed.

**The clause is right, read against `historySlotOf`:**
